subproblems.title: Coefficient-norm properties of covectors (reused comparator-accepted rsd_mw_tfa_norm_props; supplied proof step 1)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let F := Covector (Euclid P) n (continuous alternating n-linear forms on ℝ^P with the operator norm ‖·‖), and let N := covectorEuclideanNorm, i.e. N(α) = (Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P strictly increasing} α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)})²)^{1/2} for the standard orthonormal basis (e_j) of ℝ^P. Then (i) N(α + α') ≤ N(α) + N(α') for all α, α' ∈ F; (ii) N(t·α) = |t|·N(α) for all t ∈ ℝ and α ∈ F; (iii) there is a real C ≥ 0 with N(α) ≤ C·‖α‖ for all α ∈ F; and (iv) N : F → ℝ is continuous.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ), (∀ α α' : Covector (Euclid P) n, covectorEuclideanNorm (α + α') ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α + covectorEuclideanNorm α') ∧ (∀ (t : ℝ) (α : Covector (Euclid P) n), covectorEuclideanNorm (t • α) = |t| * covectorEuclideanNorm α) ∧ (∃ C : ℝ, 0 ≤ C ∧ ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, covectorEuclideanNorm α ≤ C * ‖α‖) ∧ Continuous (fun α : Covector (Euclid P) n => covectorEuclideanNorm α)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 of the supplied proof of cmc_fc_series_current (Simon Ch. 6, (1.15) and Remark 2.6: the inner-product norm of covectors, chapter-06.txt lines 178 and 243–250). This is the comparator-accepted theorem Submission.rsd_mw_tfa_norm_props (DAG node root.regular_set_dense-a1.mass_eq_weight-a1.test_form_approx-a1.norm_props-a1, candidate commit f492ba4), reused with its identical frozen type; the proof below is the one formalized there.

Notation. e_j := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ j (j ∈ Fin P) is the standard orthonormal basis of ℝ^P, so ‖e_j‖ = 1. 𝓙 is the finite type of all maps I : Fin n → Fin P, with #𝓙 = Fintype.card (Fin n → Fin P). For I ∈ 𝓙 put e_I := (e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)}), in Lean (fun i => e (I i)). F := Covector (Euclid P) n carries the operator norm ‖·‖ of continuous alternating maps. By definition N(α) := covectorEuclideanNorm α = √(Σ_{I∈𝓙} q_I(α)), where q_I(α) := α(e_I)² if I is strictly increasing and q_I(α) := 0 otherwise.

1. (Coefficient vector.) For α ∈ F and I ∈ 𝓙 put c_I(α) := α(e_I) if I is strictly increasing and c_I(α) := 0 otherwise. Since (if p then a else 0)² = (if p then a² else 0), q_I(α) = c_I(α)² for every I. Let v(α) ∈ EuclideanSpace ℝ 𝓙 be the vector with coordinates c_I(α) (in Lean, v α := WithLp.toLp 2 (fun I => c_I α)). The formula ‖w‖ = √(Σ_I ‖w_I‖²) (EuclideanSpace.norm_eq), with ‖w_I‖² = w_I², gives N(α) = ‖v(α)‖ for every α ∈ F. (∗)
2. (Linearity of v.) Evaluation at a fixed tuple is linear in the form: (α + α')(e_I) = α(e_I) + α'(e_I) and (t·α)(e_I) = t·α(e_I). Hence c_I(α + α') = c_I(α) + c_I(α') and c_I(t·α) = t·c_I(α) for every I (both sides are 0 when I is not strictly increasing), so v(α + α') = v(α) + v(α') and v(t·α) = t·v(α) (WithLp.toLp_add, WithLp.toLp_smul).
3. (Proof of (i).) By (∗), step 2 and the triangle inequality in EuclideanSpace ℝ 𝓙: N(α + α') = ‖v(α) + v(α')‖ ≤ ‖v(α)‖ + ‖v(α')‖ = N(α) + N(α').
4. (Proof of (ii).) By (∗), step 2 and homogeneity of the norm: N(t·α) = ‖t·v(α)‖ = |t|·‖v(α)‖ = |t|·N(α).
5. (Coordinate bound.) For every I ∈ 𝓙, |c_I(α)| ≤ ‖α‖: if I is strictly increasing, the operator-norm bound for continuous alternating maps (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm) gives |α(e_I)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏_k ‖e_{I(k)}‖ = ‖α‖; otherwise |c_I(α)| = 0 ≤ ‖α‖.
6. (Proof of (iii).) Put C := √(#𝓙) ≥ 0. By step 5, c_I(α)² ≤ ‖α‖² for every I, so Σ_I c_I(α)² ≤ #𝓙·‖α‖². Since √ is monotone and ‖α‖ ≥ 0, N(α) = √(Σ_I c_I(α)²) ≤ √(#𝓙·‖α‖²) = √(#𝓙)·‖α‖ = C·‖α‖.
7. (Proof of (iv).) Let α, α' ∈ F. By (i), N(α) = N((α − α') + α') ≤ N(α − α') + N(α'). Since α' − α = −(α − α') and N(−β) = N(β) (SimonGMT covectorEuclideanNorm_neg), (i) also gives N(α') ≤ N(α' − α) + N(α) = N(α − α') + N(α). Together with (iii), |N(α) − N(α')| ≤ N(α − α') ≤ C·‖α − α'‖, i.e. dist(N(α), N(α')) ≤ C·dist(α, α'). So N is Lipschitz with the nonnegative constant C (LipschitzWith.of_dist_le_mul with K := ⟨C, C ≥ 0⟩), hence continuous.
Steps 3, 4, 6 and 7 prove (i)–(iv), with C = √(Fintype.card (Fin n → Fin P)) in (iii). ∎
proof_key_steps: Write N(α) = ‖v(α)‖ for the coefficient vector v(α) = (α(e_I) if I is strictly increasing, else 0)_I in EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n → Fin P).
v is additive and ℝ-homogeneous because evaluation at a fixed tuple is linear in α; (i) and (ii) follow from the triangle inequality and homogeneity of the Euclidean norm.
|α(e_I)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏‖e_{I(k)}‖ = ‖α‖, so N(α) ≤ √(card(Fin n → Fin P))·‖α‖, which is (iii).
|N(α) − N(α')| ≤ N(α − α') ≤ C‖α − α'‖, so N is Lipschitz and hence continuous, which is (iv).

subproblems.title: Test-form convergence to 0 gives uniform smallness (reused comparator-accepted dpf_pfc_testFormOnConverges_zero_uniform; supplied proof step 7)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P any set, and (ω_j)_{j∈ℕ} a sequence in 𝒟ⁿ(U) (TestFormOn U n) with TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0, i.e. there is a compact K ⊆ U containing tsupport ω_j for every j such that every iterated derivative of ω_j converges uniformly on K to that of 0. Then there is a compact C ⊆ U such that ω_j(x) = 0 for every j and every x ∉ C, and for every ε > 0, for all sufficiently large j, ‖ω_j(x)‖ ≤ ε for every x ∈ ℝ^P (‖·‖ the operator norm on n-covectors, ω_j(x) := (ω_j : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (ωs : ℕ → TestFormOn U n), TestFormOnConverges ωs 0 → ∃ C : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact C ∧ C ⊆ U ∧ (∀ j x, x ∉ C → (ωs j : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x = 0) ∧ ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ j in atTop, ∀ x, ‖(ωs j : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x‖ ≤ ε
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the first half of step 7 of the supplied proof of cmc_fc_series_current (Simon Ch. 6, §1, the topology of 𝒟ⁿ(U), chapter-06.txt lines 170–176, used with β = 0). This is the comparator-accepted theorem Submission.dpf_pfc_testFormOnConverges_zero_uniform (DAG node root.minimizing_implies_stationary-a1.diffeo_pushforward-a1.pushforward_current-a1.uniform_small-a1, candidate commit 8d68dfd), reused with its identical frozen type; the proof below is the one formalized there. Notation: ω_j(x) := (ωs j : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x, and ‖·‖ is the operator norm on Covector (Euclid P) n.
1. (Unfolding.) By definition of TestFormOnConverges ωs 0 there is C ⊆ ℝ^P such that C is compact, C ⊆ U, tsupport ω_j ⊆ C for every j (and tsupport 0 ⊆ C, not needed), and for every k ∈ ℕ, iteratedFDeriv ℝ k ω_j → iteratedFDeriv ℝ k 0 uniformly on C as j → ∞. Take this C; it gives the first two conjuncts.
2. (Vanishing off C.) Let x ∉ C and j ∈ ℕ. Since tsupport ω_j ⊆ C, x ∉ tsupport ω_j, so ω_j(x) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport). This is the third conjunct.
3. (The case k = 0.) The zero test form coerces to the zero form, so iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 0 x = 0 for every x. Let ε > 0. Uniform convergence for k = 0 (Metric.tendstoUniformlyOn_iff) gives j₀ such that for all j ≥ j₀ and all x ∈ C, dist(iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 0 x, iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 ω_j x) < ε, i.e. ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 ω_j x‖ < ε. Since ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 f x‖ = ‖f(x)‖ (norm_iteratedFDeriv_zero), ‖ω_j(x)‖ < ε, hence ‖ω_j(x)‖ ≤ ε, for j ≥ j₀ and x ∈ C.
4. (Points off C.) For j ≥ j₀ and x ∉ C, step 2 gives ‖ω_j(x)‖ = 0 ≤ ε.
5. (Conclusion.) For every ε > 0 and all sufficiently large j (∀ᶠ j in atTop), ‖ω_j(x)‖ ≤ ε for every x ∈ ℝ^P. With steps 1–2, C satisfies all four conjuncts. ∎
proof_key_steps: Unfold TestFormOnConverges: a compact C ⊆ U contains every tsupport ω_j, and all iterated derivatives converge uniformly on C.
k = 0 and ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 f x‖ = ‖f x‖ give, eventually, ‖ω_j(x)‖ < ε on C.
Combine: eventually ‖ω_j(x)‖ ≤ ε for all x.

subproblems.title: A test form has bounded Euclidean coefficient norm (Simon 6.1.15; supplied proof step 2)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P any set and ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). Then there is a real number c > 0 such that |ω(x)| ≤ c for every x ∈ ℝ^P. Conventions: 𝒟ⁿ(U) = TestFormOn U n is the real submodule of smooth (ContDiff ℝ ∞) n-forms on ℝ^P with compact support and tsupport ⊆ U, and ω(x) denotes (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x; |α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P strictly increasing} α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)})²)^{1/2} is the Euclidean coefficient norm of an n-covector α (e the standard orthonormal basis of ℝ^P) and ‖α‖ its operator norm as a continuous alternating map; 𝒟_n(U) = GeometricCurrentOn U n is the space of n-currents in U (an ℝ-linear map toCurrent : 𝒟ⁿ(U) → ℝ, applied as X(ω), together with sequential continuity: X(ω_j) → 0 whenever TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0); M(X) = X.mass = X.massOn U ∈ [0, ∞] is the supremum of ENNReal.ofReal X(ω) over ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n U, i.e. over ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ U and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (ω : TestFormOn U n), ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) ≤ c
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the supplied proof of cmc_fc_series_current (Simon Ch. 6, (1.15): |ω| = sup_x |ω(x)| is finite for ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), chapter-06.txt lines 170–178). Notation: N(α) := covectorEuclideanNorm α; for ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), ω(x) := (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x. The sibling theorem norm_props is Submission.rsd_mw_tfa_norm_props; only its conjunct (iv) (continuity of N) is used.
1. (Regularity of ω.) By definition of the submodule TestFormOn U n, ω ∈ TestFormOn U n means IsTestForm ω ∧ tsupport ω ⊆ U, where IsTestForm ω = IsSmoothForm ω ∧ HasCompactSupport ω and IsSmoothForm ω = ContDiff ℝ ∞ ω. A C^∞ map is continuous (ContDiff.continuous), so x ↦ ω(x) is a continuous map ℝ^P → Covector (Euclid P) n with compact support.
2. (The function g.) Put g(x) := N(ω(x)). By norm_props (iv) applied to P and n, α ↦ N(α) is continuous, so g = N ∘ ω is continuous. Since N(0) = 0 (SimonGMT covectorEuclideanNorm_zero), g(x) = 0 whenever ω(x) = 0; hence g has compact support (HasCompactSupport.comp_left with g 0 = 0).
3. (Boundedness.) A continuous real-valued function with compact support is bounded (Mathlib Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support): there is C ∈ ℝ with ‖g(x)‖ ≤ C for every x. Since ‖g(x)‖ = |g(x)| ≥ g(x), we get g(x) ≤ C for every x.
4. (A positive bound.) Put c := max(C, 0) + 1. Then c ≥ 1 > 0, and g(x) ≤ C ≤ max(C, 0) < c for every x ∈ ℝ^P, i.e. N(ω(x)) ≤ c for all x. This c witnesses the claim. ∎
Lean note (a compiled route, about 15 lines): `have hsmooth : IsSmoothForm (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) := ω.property.1.1`; `(hnorm P n).2.2.2.comp (ContDiff.continuous hsmooth)` (IsSmoothForm unfolds definitionally to ContDiff ℝ ∞; do not `open scoped ContDiff`, which turns `ω` into a reserved token); `HasCompactSupport.comp_left (g := covectorEuclideanNorm) ω.property.1.2 (covectorEuclideanNorm_zero P n)`; `obtain ⟨C, hC⟩ := hcont.bounded_above_of_compact_support hcs`; `refine ⟨max C 0 + 1, by positivity, fun x => ?_⟩`; finish with `Real.norm_eq_abs`, `le_abs_self`, `le_max_left` and `linarith`.
proof_key_steps: ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) is ContDiff ℝ ∞, hence continuous, and has compact support.
x ↦ |ω(x)| is continuous (norm_props (iv)) and has compact support because |0| = 0.
A continuous compactly supported real function is bounded by some C.
c := max(C, 0) + 1 > 0 bounds |ω(x)| for all x.

subproblems.title: Evaluation of a finite-mass current is bounded by mass times the coefficient sup norm (Simon 6.2.4; supplied proof step 3)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P any set, X ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with M(X) ≠ ∞, ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), and c ∈ ℝ with c > 0 and |ω(x)| ≤ c for every x ∈ ℝ^P. Then |X(ω)| ≤ c·M(X)^ℝ, where M(X)^ℝ := M(X).toReal. Conventions: 𝒟ⁿ(U) = TestFormOn U n is the real submodule of smooth (ContDiff ℝ ∞) n-forms on ℝ^P with compact support and tsupport ⊆ U, and ω(x) denotes (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x; |α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P strictly increasing} α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)})²)^{1/2} is the Euclidean coefficient norm of an n-covector α (e the standard orthonormal basis of ℝ^P) and ‖α‖ its operator norm as a continuous alternating map; 𝒟_n(U) = GeometricCurrentOn U n is the space of n-currents in U (an ℝ-linear map toCurrent : 𝒟ⁿ(U) → ℝ, applied as X(ω), together with sequential continuity: X(ω_j) → 0 whenever TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0); M(X) = X.mass = X.massOn U ∈ [0, ∞] is the supremum of ENNReal.ofReal X(ω) over ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n U, i.e. over ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ U and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (X : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (ω : TestFormOn U n) (c : ℝ), 0 < c → X.mass ≠ ∞ → (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) ≤ c) → |X ω| ≤ c * X.mass.toReal
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 of the supplied proof of cmc_fc_series_current; Simon Ch. 6, (2.4) M(T) = sup_{|ω| ≤ 1, ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U)} T(ω) (chapter-06.txt lines 220–226), which gives |T(ω)| ≤ |ω|·M(T), the estimate Simon uses for the M-absolutely convergent series in the proof of 7.2 (chapter-06.txt lines 2119–2123). Notation: N(α) := covectorEuclideanNorm α; ω(x) := (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x; M := X.mass ∈ [0, ∞] and M^ℝ := M.toReal. Hypotheses: c > 0, M ≠ ∞, and N(ω(x)) ≤ c for every x ∈ ℝ^P. The sibling theorem norm_props is Submission.rsd_mw_tfa_norm_props; only its conjunct (ii) (N(t·α) = |t|·N(α)) is used.
1. (Admissible rescalings.) Let s ∈ ℝ with |s| = c⁻¹. Since TestFormOn U n is a real submodule, s•ω ∈ TestFormOn U n, and its membership gives tsupport (s•ω) ⊆ U. As a form, (s•ω)(x) = s•ω(x) for every x (the submodule coercion commutes with scalar multiplication; this holds definitionally). By norm_props (ii), N((s•ω)(x)) = |s|·N(ω(x)) = c⁻¹·N(ω(x)) ≤ c⁻¹·c = 1, using N(ω(x)) ≤ c and c⁻¹ ≥ 0. Hence s•ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n U (tsupport ⊆ U and N ≤ 1 everywhere).
2. (Evaluation bounded by mass.) By SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn, ENNReal.ofReal (X(s•ω)) ≤ X.massOn U, and X.massOn U = X.mass = M by the definition of mass. Since M ≠ ∞, ENNReal.ofReal_le_iff_le_toReal turns this into X(s•ω) ≤ M^ℝ.
3. (Linearity.) X(s•ω) = s·X(ω), because X.toCurrent is ℝ-linear (map_smul, smul_eq_mul). Hence s·X(ω) ≤ M^ℝ for every s ∈ ℝ with |s| = c⁻¹.
4. (Both signs.) Since c > 0, |c⁻¹| = c⁻¹ and |−c⁻¹| = c⁻¹. Step 3 with s = c⁻¹ gives c⁻¹·X(ω) ≤ M^ℝ; multiplying by c > 0 gives X(ω) ≤ c·M^ℝ. Step 3 with s = −c⁻¹ gives −c⁻¹·X(ω) ≤ M^ℝ; multiplying by c gives −X(ω) ≤ c·M^ℝ. By abs_le, |X(ω)| ≤ c·M^ℝ = c·X.mass.toReal. ∎
Lean note (a compiled route, about 35 lines): for admissibility use `refine ⟨(s • ω).property.2, fun x => ?_⟩` and `have hx : ((s • ω : TestFormOn U n) : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x = s • ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) := rfl`, then `rw [hx, hhom, hs]` and `mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left`, `inv_mul_cancel₀`; `X.le_massOn hadm : ENNReal.ofReal (X (s • ω)) ≤ X.massOn U` is accepted at type `≤ X.mass` by definitional unfolding; `rw [ENNReal.ofReal_le_iff_le_toReal hX] at h1`; `rw [map_smul, smul_eq_mul]` for X (s • ω) = s * X ω; finish with `abs_le`, `field_simp` and `linarith`.
proof_key_steps: For |s| = c⁻¹, s•ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) has tsupport ⊆ U and |s•ω(x)| = c⁻¹|ω(x)| ≤ 1 (norm_props (ii)), so it is admissible for M = M_U.
GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn and M ≠ ∞ give X(s•ω) ≤ M.toReal.
Linearity gives s·X(ω) ≤ M.toReal.
s = ±c⁻¹ gives ±X(ω) ≤ c·M.toReal, i.e. |X(ω)| ≤ c·M.toReal.

subproblems.title: A linear functional on test forms dominated by the coefficient sup norm is a current (supplied proof step 7; the bound of step 6 is its hypothesis)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P any set, L : 𝒟ⁿ(U) → ℝ an ℝ-linear map (TestFormOn U n →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ) and A ∈ ℝ such that |L(ω)| ≤ c·A whenever ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), c ∈ ℝ, c > 0 and |ω(x)| ≤ c for every x ∈ ℝ^P. Then there is a current Y ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with Y(ω) = L(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). Conventions: 𝒟ⁿ(U) = TestFormOn U n is the real submodule of smooth (ContDiff ℝ ∞) n-forms on ℝ^P with compact support and tsupport ⊆ U, and ω(x) denotes (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x; |α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P strictly increasing} α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)})²)^{1/2} is the Euclidean coefficient norm of an n-covector α (e the standard orthonormal basis of ℝ^P) and ‖α‖ its operator norm as a continuous alternating map; 𝒟_n(U) = GeometricCurrentOn U n is the space of n-currents in U (an ℝ-linear map toCurrent : 𝒟ⁿ(U) → ℝ, applied as X(ω), together with sequential continuity: X(ω_j) → 0 whenever TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0); M(X) = X.mass = X.massOn U ∈ [0, ∞] is the supremum of ENNReal.ofReal X(ω) over ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n U, i.e. over ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ U and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (L : TestFormOn U n →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ) (A : ℝ), (∀ (ω : TestFormOn U n) (c : ℝ), 0 < c → (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) ≤ c) → |L ω| ≤ c * A) → ∃ Y : GeometricCurrentOn U n, ∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, Y ω = L ω
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 7 of the supplied proof of cmc_fc_series_current, whose step-6 bound is the hypothesis (H) below (Simon Ch. 6, proof of 7.2: the M-absolutely convergent series "define" currents, chapter-06.txt lines 2119–2123; the topology of 𝒟ⁿ(U), chapter-06.txt lines 170–176). This isolates the fact that a linear functional bounded by A·sup_x |ω(x)| is sequentially continuous, i.e. a current. Notation: N(α) := covectorEuclideanNorm α; ω(x) := (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x; ‖·‖ is the operator norm on Covector (Euclid P) n. Hypothesis (H): |L(ω)| ≤ c·A whenever ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), c > 0 and N(ω(x)) ≤ c for all x. Sibling theorems: norm_props = Submission.rsd_mw_tfa_norm_props (only conjunct (iii) is used) and uniform_small = Submission.dpf_pfc_testFormOnConverges_zero_uniform.
1. (A ≥ 0.) Apply (H) to ω = 0 and c = 1. The zero test form has N(0(x)) = N(0) = 0 ≤ 1 (SimonGMT covectorEuclideanNorm_zero), and L(0) = 0 by linearity, so 0 = |L(0)| ≤ 1·A = A.
2. (The constant C.) By norm_props (iii) applied to P and n, there is C ∈ ℝ with C ≥ 0 and N(α) ≤ C·‖α‖ for every α ∈ Covector (Euclid P) n.
3. (Sequential continuity of L.) Let ωs : ℕ → 𝒟ⁿ(U) with TestFormOnConverges ωs 0. By uniform_small (applied to P, n, U, ωs), for every ε > 0, for all sufficiently large j, ‖ωs_j(x)‖ ≤ ε for all x. Let η > 0 and put ε := η / (2(C + 1)(A + 1)); then ε > 0, since η > 0, C + 1 ≥ 1 and A + 1 ≥ 1 (steps 1–2). Choose j₀ with ‖ωs_j(x)‖ ≤ ε for all j ≥ j₀ and all x. For j ≥ j₀ and every x, N(ωs_j(x)) ≤ C·‖ωs_j(x)‖ ≤ C·ε ≤ (C + 1)·ε, using C ≥ 0 and ε > 0. Since (C + 1)·ε > 0, (H) with c := (C + 1)·ε gives |L(ωs_j)| ≤ (C + 1)·ε·A. Now (C + 1)·ε·(A + 1) = η/2, and (C + 1)·ε > 0 with A ≤ A + 1, so (C + 1)·ε·A ≤ (C + 1)·ε·(A + 1) = η/2 < η. Hence dist(L(ωs_j), 0) = |L(ωs_j)| < η for all j ≥ j₀. Since η > 0 was arbitrary, L(ωs_j) → 0 as j → ∞ (Metric.tendsto_atTop). (This is the estimate of step 7 of the supplied proof, |Y(ω_k)| ≤ (N·ε_k + 1/(k+1))·s → 0, written with an explicit ε and j₀.)
4. (The current.) A GeometricCurrentOn U n is a structure with fields toCurrent : TestFormOn U n →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ and continuous' : for every ωs with TestFormOnConverges ωs 0, toCurrent(ωs_j) → 0 in ℝ. Step 3 is exactly continuous' for toCurrent := L. Put Y := ⟨L, step 3⟩. Its coercion to a function is Y.toCurrent = L, so Y(ω) = L(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (definitionally). ∎
Lean note (a compiled route, about 30 lines): `obtain ⟨C, hC0, hC⟩ := (hnorm P n).2.2.1`; `have hA : 0 ≤ A := by simpa using hL 0 1 one_pos (fun x => by simp)`; `refine ⟨⟨L, fun ωs hωs => ?_⟩, fun ω => rfl⟩`; `obtain ⟨K, -, -, -, hunif⟩ := hsmall P n U ωs hωs`; `rw [Metric.tendsto_atTop]`; `set ε : ℝ := η / (2 * (C + 1) * (A + 1))`; `obtain ⟨N, hN⟩ := eventually_atTop.mp (hunif ε hεpos)`; bound N(ωs_j(x)) with `hC`, `mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left` and `nlinarith`; `rw [Real.dist_eq, sub_zero]`; `field_simp` proves (C + 1) * ε * (A + 1) = η / 2, and `nlinarith` closes (C + 1) * ε * A < η.
proof_key_steps: (H) at ω = 0, c = 1 gives A ≥ 0; norm_props (iii) gives C ≥ 0 with |α| ≤ C‖α‖.
If ωs → 0 in 𝒟ⁿ(U), uniform_small gives eventually ‖ωs_j(x)‖ ≤ ε for all x, hence |ωs_j(x)| ≤ (C + 1)ε.
(H) gives |L(ωs_j)| ≤ (C + 1)εA ≤ η/2 < η for ε = η/(2(C + 1)(A + 1)), so L(ωs_j) → 0.
Y := ⟨L, continuity⟩ is a current with Y(ω) = L(ω).
